1.text: ↑ This book is scarcely entitled to a place among the Sibylline Oracles, or to be called a book. It is a brief hymn in honor of Christ and the cross, and probably of later date than any other portion of the present collection.
↑ 10. Pure flower.—Cited by Lactantius, Div. Inst., iv, 18 (L., 6, 486), and comp. Isa. xi, 1, 2, where the Septuagint reads blossom.
↑ 16–19. Cited by Lactantius, Div. Inst., iv, 15 [L., 6, 494].
↑ 20. Child.—Or a plant; a shoot. Comp. Isa. xi, 1.
↑ 26. Sodomitic land.—Judea, so called on account of her wickedness. Comp. Isa. i, 10; Ezek, xvi, 48, 49.
↑ 27–31. Cited by Lactantius, Div. Inst., iv, 18 [L., 6, 507].
↑ 38. Cited by Sozomen, Hist. Eccl., ii, 1 [G., 67, 933].
